Splitting by cheapest cleared vendor per line covers 9 of 10 lines and costs about Rs 10.11 million in total. This uses only rows that are comparable and cleared the questionnaire, and all 5 vendors have replied.

Awards:
- RM-001: V01, Rs 321.9/kg
- RM-002: V03, Rs 112.0/kg
- RM-003: V02, Rs 1,138.8/kg
- RM-004: V02, Rs 1,914.5/kg
- RM-005: V02, Rs 1,695.6/kg
- RM-006: V02, Rs 956.4/kg
- RM-007: V01, Rs 1,080/kg
- RM-009: V04, Rs 25,145.8/kg
- RM-010: V04, Rs 15,506.6/kg

RM-008 (rosemary extract) dropped out. No cleared, comparable quote exists for it, so it needs a separate decision. The total excludes it and is not a full-basket cost.

Clearing the questionnaire does not make these awards safe:
- **V02** wins four lines (RM-003 to RM-006). Each carries CLAIM_CONTRADICTED and WITHHELD flags. RM-003 also has COA_STALE, and RM-004 also has STRENGTH_ADJUSTED. V02's OTIF on these lines is 0.75–0.80. Its defect rate is as high as 6.6% on RM-003.
- **V04** wins RM-009 and RM-010, which are the bulk of the spend. Both are flagged LATE, MOQ_COVER and SPACE_CLASH, and RM-009 also has COA_CONFLICT. The lines are 36 days late, and V04 has no OTIF or defect history. That lack of history is not evidence of poor performance, but it is unproven.
- **V01 and V03** win RM-001, RM-002 and RM-007. They have no risk flags and arrive early, with OTIF of 0.95 or better on the V01 lines.

The cheapest-per-line split pushes most of the risk onto V02 and V04. The 36-day lateness on RM-009 and RM-010 is a real threat to the 20 December need-by date.
